Categories, classes and shoot-offs

Besides the open ranking, where everyone competes together, FITASC events rank shooters in categories by age and sex. From 1 January 2027 the international table for Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ and Compak® Sporting has six categories. They are Junior (13–20), Lady (from 13), Men (21–55), Senior (56–65), Veteran (66–72) and Master (from 73, men and women). For events before that date, check the table then in force on the FITASC website.

What counts is the year of birth, not the birthday. A shooter moves into a new category on 1 January of the year in which he or she reaches its lowest age, for example 56 for Senior. This holds even if the birthday is in December. For the 2027 season this means: Junior born 2007–2014, Men born 1972–2006, Senior 1962–1971, Veteran 1955–1961, Master born before 1955. Each new season all these year ranges move on by one year.

Note that Senior is not the main adult category but the 56–65 age group; the main adult category is Men (Homme in French). One score counts in the open ranking and in your category at the same time, so it can win a medal in both.

Men and women shoot from the same stands at the same targets: there are no special trajectories or shorter distances for women. The category changes only the ranking you appear in, and some women finish high in the open ranking too.

The women’s category is Lady (Dame in French). It is open from the year a girl turns 13 and has no upper age limit. A girl aged 13–20 is also of Junior age; the competition rules and the programme say which category she enters.

In special cases a shooter may be allowed to compete in a category other than the one their age gives; this permission is called a derogation. If you think you need one, ask your national federation.

Teams have their own rules: a team usually has three shooters; the Men team in Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ has four. A junior placed in the Men team, or a junior girl in the Lady team, must also enter that category individually. National federations and clubs may use their own categories, so always check the competition programme. Each category has its own medals. In Compak® Sporting the categories also have shoot-offs for their top three. So there can be a shoot-off for, say, third place in the Veteran category as well as in the open ranking. In Sporting™ the programme says whether categories have shoot-offs.

Who may join which team: the Men team may include junior boys and Senior, Veteran and Master shooters; the Lady team, women or junior girls. A Senior team may also include Veteran and Master shooters.

Classes are different. In some countries shooters are put into classes, such as AA, A, B and C, by their average scores, so that people of a similar level compete together. A category depends on age or sex, a class on results. The international FITASC rules set no classes for shooters (the A, B and C classes in the Sporting™ rules grade trajectories, not people).

An international event is 200 targets in rounds of 25. When shooters tie for one of the first three places, they shoot a shoot-off of 25 targets. If they are still level, sudden death follows: they keep shooting, and the first shooter to miss (score a zero) is out. Below third place there is no shoot-off: tied shooters share the place, and countback sets their order in the list. Their scores are compared on the 8th layout or Compak first, then on the 7th, and so on back to the 1st; the first difference decides who is listed higher. Teams do not shoot off; tied teams are also separated by countback, using their members’ combined scores.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

If time allows, the shoot-off is shot on a new layout set by the jury. The usual rules apply.

Compak® Sporting

Shoot-offs decide the top three in the open ranking and in each category. They are shot on a Compak with one single and two simultaneous doubles at each station. If the shooters who tied in the open ranking are also from the same category, that one shoot-off decides their order in the category too.

Stay close if you might be in a shoot-off. If no time was set in advance, keep in touch with the jury: you must be ready to shoot within 15 minutes of the call. A shooter who is not there is out, and nobody takes that place: the others shoot the shoot-off without them. For exceptional reasons the jury may move the shoot-off to the next day.

An example: two shooters tie on 188 for 5th place. They share the place, and countback lists them in order: it compares their scores on the 8th layout or Compak first, then on the 7th, and so on back to the 1st. If one shot 24 on the 8th layout and the other 23, the first is listed above the second. Tied teams are separated in the same way, by their members’ combined scores.

Tip: Many coaches suggest keeping your usual routine and pace in a shoot-off, even when spectators gather round. More: Pressure and choking: why easy targets get missed.

Key points

  • Year of birth decides; the new category starts on 1 January
  • Senior = 56–65, not “adults”; the main adult category is Men
  • Ties for places 1–3: 25-target shoot-off, then sudden death
  • Below 3rd: countback from the 8th layout or Compak; no team shoot-offs
  • Might you be in a shoot-off? Stay close and be ready within 15 minutes of the call.

Did you know?

In Sporting™ sudden death a double on report counts as a pair. Hit-then-miss (“one-zero”) is the same as miss-then-hit (“zero-one”), so it does not matter which of the two targets you lost.

Stand Talk

  • Referee Which category are you shooting in?

    Meaning: Asked at registration: Junior, Lady, Men, Senior, Veteran or Master.

  • Referee He’s a Senior now.

    Meaning: He is in the 56–65 group this season.

  • Referee She won the Lady category and was fourth overall.

    Meaning: First among ladies, fourth in the open ranking.

  • Referee There’s a shoot-off for Veteran bronze.

    Meaning: Compak® Sporting (or a Sporting™ event whose programme has category shoot-offs): two or more Veterans are tied for third in their category.

  • Referee There’s a tie for third — shoot-off in fifteen minutes.

    Meaning: Be at the named layout and ready to shoot within fifteen minutes.

  • Referee Sudden death: first zero is out.

    Meaning: After the 25-target shoot-off, the first shooter to miss (with an equal number of targets shot) is eliminated.

For the interpreter
  • The biggest interpreter trap is “Senior”. In many sports “senior” means the adult level (as opposed to junior), but in FITASC Senior is the 56–65 age group; the main adult category is Men. Do not translate it with the word for adults in your language. “Master” is another trap: the FITASC age category from 73 has nothing to do with the NSCA “Master class”, which is a skill level.
  • Shoot-offs bring one more interpreter trap. If no time was fixed, the shooters must be ready within fifteen minutes of the call. A missing shooter is “disqualified” in the Sporting™ rules and “considered withdrawn” in the Compak® Sporting rules. Use the word of the discipline you are at.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. How does a category differ from a class?

    1. They mean the same thing in the rules
    2. A category is by results, a class by age
    3. A category is by age or sex, a class by results
    Answer

    A category is by age or sex, a class by results

    Junior, Lady, Senior and Veteran are categories by age or sex; AA, A, B and C are national classes by average score.

  2. How are tied shooters below third place ranked?

    1. They share it; countback from the 8th layout sets the order
    2. By a shoot-off of 25 targets for the place
    3. By drawing lots after the event has ended
    Answer

    They share it; countback from the 8th layout sets the order

    There are no shoot-offs below third place: the place is shared and countback sets the order, from the 8th layout or Compak back to the 1st.

    Chapter 18 · Shoot-off for the top three; ties below

  3. A shooter born in 1971 enters a FITASC competition in 2027. Which category?

    1. Men
    2. Senior
    3. Veteran
    4. Master
    Answer

    Senior

    He turns 56 in 2027, so he is Senior from 1 January, whatever his birthday.

    Senior
